assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Fix arbitrary n, k, l in the allowed range and assume the quotient is polynomial. Replace k and l by k0 = min(k, n-k) and l0 = min(l, n-l) using q-binomial symmetry, and use the degree obstruction to force l0 <= k0. Rewrite the reduced quotient as a shifted interval ratio F_{b,m,d}(q) with b = l0, m = k0 - l0, and d = n - k0 - l0. The cyclotomic exponent formula converts polynomiality of F_{b,m,d}(q) into the floor-count condition saying that every modulus t sees at least as many multiples in the shifted numerator interval as in the denominator interval. The bottleneck positivity lemma for shifted interval ratios then shows that F_{b,m,d}(q), hence the original quotient, has nonnegative coefficients. Finally discharge the temporary polynomiality hypothesis and generalize over n, k, l.

steps.derives: Let k0 := min(k, n-k) and l0 := min(l, n-l). Then [n choose k]_q = [n choose k0]_q and [n choose l]_q = [n choose l0]_q, so [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q = [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q. In particular, H implies that the reduced quotient [n choose k0]_q / [n choose l0]_q is also a polynomial in q.
steps.trivial_justification: Because k0 is either k or n-k, L1 gives [n choose k]_q = [n choose k0]_q; similarly, because l0 is either l or n-l, L1 gives [n choose l]_q = [n choose l0]_q. Substituting these two equalities into the quotient gives equality of the original and reduced rational functions. Since H says the original quotient is polynomial, the reduced quotient is polynomial as well.

steps.derives: The reduced indices satisfy k0 >= l0.
steps.trivial_justification: L2 applies directly to the same integers n, k, and l under the hypothesis H and yields min(k, n-k) >= min(l, n-l), which is exactly k0 >= l0.

steps.derives: From the definitions of k0 and l0, we have 0 <= k0 <= n/2 and 0 <= l0 <= n/2; together with A2 this gives 0 <= l0 <= k0 <= n/2. Define b := l0, m := k0 - l0, and d := n - k0 - l0. Then b, m, and d are nonnegative integers.
steps.trivial_justification: By definition of minimum, both k0 and l0 are at most n/2 and are nonnegative. A2 gives l0 <= k0, so m = k0 - l0 >= 0. Also d = n - k0 - l0 >= 0 because k0 <= n/2 and l0 <= n/2 imply k0 + l0 <= n. Hence b, m, d are all valid inputs for the shifted interval product.

steps.trivial_justification: A3 gives exactly the hypotheses 0 <= l0 <= k0 <= n/2 needed for L3. Applying L3 with l = l0 and k = k0 rewrites the reduced quotient in the stated shifted interval form; because b = l0, m = k0 - l0, and d = n - k0 - l0, this rewritten product is exactly F_{b,m,d}(q).

lemmas.statement_nl: For integers b, m, and d with b >= 0, m >= 0, and d >= 0, define F_{b,m,d}(q) := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when m = 0. For each positive integer t, the exponent of the cyclotomic polynomial Phi_t(q) in the factorization of the rational function F_{b,m,d}(q) is (floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t)) - (floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t)). Consequently, F_{b,m,d}(q) is a polynomial in q if and only if floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t) for every positive integer t; in that case F_{b,m,d}(q) actually lies in Z[q].

payload.theorem_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Unlike the rejected draft, the outer universal quantifiers and the temporary implication hypothesis are opened and closed in separate assembly steps. After fixing arbitrary n, then k with 0 <= k <= n, then l with 0 <= l <= n, and finally a temporary polynomiality hypothesis H, we replace k and l by k0 = min(k, n-k) and l0 = min(l, n-l) using q-binomial symmetry. Polynomiality forces k0 >= l0, so the reduced quotient can be rewritten as a shifted interval ratio F_{b,m,d}(q) with b = l0, m = k0 - l0, and d = n - k0 - l0; moreover 2k0 <= n gives d >= m, so only that subfamily of shifted ratios is needed. Cyclotomic exponent counting converts polynomiality of F_{b,m,d}(q) into the floor-count condition on multiples in two intervals. The explicit bottleneck lemma then proves coefficientwise nonnegativity of F_{b,m,d}(q) on this d >= m subfamily. Equality transfers the nonnegativity first to the reduced quotient and then to the original quotient. Finally the temporary hypothesis H is discharged, and the variables l, k, and n are generalized one at a time to recover exactly the theorem.

steps.trivial_justification: Since k0 = min(k, n-k), we have k0 >= 0, k0 <= k, and k0 <= n-k. Adding the last two inequalities gives 2k0 <= n, hence k0 <= n/2. lemmas.statement_nl: For integers n, k, and l with 0 <= l <= k <= n/2, define [n choose r]_q := product_{j=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+j)) / (1 - q^j) for 0 <= r <= n, with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Set m := k-l and d := n-k-l. Then [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q = product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(l+d+i)) / (1 - q^(l+i)), where the product is interpreted as 1 when m = 0.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: This is a direct algebraic cancellation identity and contains no positivity argument.

lemmas.statement_nl: For integers b, m, and d with b >= 0, m >= 0, and d >= 0, define F_{b,m,d}(q) := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when m = 0. For each positive integer t, let Phi_t(q) denote the t-th cyclotomic polynomial. Then the exponent of Phi_t(q) in the cyclotomic factorization of the rational function F_{b,m,d}(q) is (floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t)) - (floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t)). Consequently, F_{b,m,d}(q) is a polynomial in q if and only if floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t) for every positive integer t; in that case F_{b,m,d}(q) actually lies in Z[q].
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: This is a cyclotomic factor-counting statement about divisibility, independent of any coefficientwise positivity.

lemmas.bottleneck_reason: After symmetry reduction and product rewriting, the root theorem becomes a positivity statement for shifted interval ratios. The assembly only ever produces parameters with d >= m, so the hard core is to prove that the floor-count condition forces coefficientwise nonnegativity on this transformed subfamily. This remains the substantive frontier step.

lemmas.statement_nl: For integers b, m, and d with b >= 0, m >= 0, and d >= m, define F_{b,m,d}(q) := product_{i=1}^m (1 - q^(b+d+i)) / (1 - q^(b+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when m = 0. Assume that for every positive integer t one has floor((b+m)/t) - floor(b/t) <= floor((b+d+m)/t) - floor((b+d)/t). Then F_{b,m,d}(q) lies in Z[q], and every coefficient in its standard expansion as a polynomial in q is a nonnegative integer.
